Assistance for National games
*741. SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA
SEKAR REDDY: Will the Minister of
YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be
pleased to state:
(a) what monetary support and other
facilities are given to a State for organising
national and international games;
(b) the assistance given and proposed to
be given to Andhra Pradesh for preparation
of the 32nd National Games 2002;
(c) whether there is any proposal to
ensure continued utilisation of sports
equipment being procured;  and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Central University in Bodoland area
*742. SHRI URKHAO GWRA
BRAHMA: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE  DEVELOPMENT be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have any plan
to set up a Central University in Assam,
particularly in the Bodoland area;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Grants to NGOs
*743. DR. ALLADI P. RAJKUMAR:
SHRI YADLAPATI VENKAT
RAO:
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS
AND SPORTS be pleased to state:
(a) what are the items for which grants
are given by the Ministry to NGOs;
(b) whether a number of NGO
proposals, received from Srikakulam District
in Andhra Pradesh, during the last two years
are pending;
(c) if so, the reasons for their pendency;
(d) the reasons for rejection/delay in
clearing of the proposals; and
(e) the steps proposed to be taken to
expedite clearance of their proposals?
Status of schemes under OBB and
Education for All
*744. PROF. M. SANKARALINGAM:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the details and the status of 'Operation
Black Board' and 'Education for All'
schemes under the Ministry;

226
WIN2\SESSION\1028RS 226
(b) the aims and objectives of these
schemes under implementation by the
Ministry; and
(c) whether Government have achieved
the desired goals?
Deaths due to pesticide exposure
*745. SHRI B. J. PANDA:
SHRI NANA DESHMUKH:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's attention has
been drawn to the report which appeared in
The Times of India of 29th April, 2002, that
500 farmers died of pesticide exposure in
AP and 1000 were exposed to related health
hazards;
(b) if so, the details of the case;
(c) whether this case has been given to a
fact finding team, if so, the details of terms
of reference;
(d) whether there were similar incidents
earlier in AP or other States, if so, the details
thereof; and
(e) whether cases of deformed babies
and gynaecological problems in women
have also been reported in Warangal district?
Roll on and Roll off systems in the
Railways
*746. DR. ARUN KUMAR SARMA:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased
to state:
(a) the objectives and the achievements
of Roll on and Roll off (Ro-Ro) system
introduced in Konkan Railway and its
advantages over normal goods traffic;
(b) whether the Railways propose to
consider experimental introduction of this
system in NF Railway, by declaration of tea
as a preferential traffic, like coal, to avail
huge tea traffic of the region;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Lok Jumbish Project for elementary
education
*747. SHRI K.M. KHAN: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether the new phase of Lok
Jumbish Project has become operational;
(b) if so, what are the targets fixed and
achievements made under the Project, as on
31st March, 2002;
(c) whether there is any proposal to
revamp the project for achieving desirable
goal of universal elementary education;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) the total amount sanctioned and spent
under the scheme?
Air pollution in Bangalore
*748. SHRI K. RAHMAN KHAN:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT
AND FORESTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether any study has been
conducted to find out average pollution
levels in major cities of the countries, if so,
the details thereof;
(b) whether Government are aware that
air pollution is alarming in Bangalore; and
(c) if so, what are the guidelines and
measures taken by Government to control
air pollution, caused due to increasing
number of vehicles?

DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:

increased agriculture productivity by 2020,
Indian Agriculture Research Institute has
come with a new variety of wheat;

of wheat, it is possible to achieve 15-20 per

New research labs
†5401. SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH
'LALAN':
SHRI KAPIL SIBAL:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether new research labs have been
set up in the country during the last three
years in order to promote agricultural
research;
(b) if so, the names of the places where
such agricultural research labs have been
set up during the said period;
(c) the total number of research labs
where research work has been conducted
by the end of March, 2002; and
(d) the total number and names of the
new foodgrain items on which research
work is being conducted in such research
labs?
Curbing the use of pesticides
5402. SHRI C. O. POULOSE: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that use of
pesticides has gone up by several times in
the last few decades;
(b) whether Government have any
information about the excessive use of
pesticides in agriculture and allied
production, food and food products; and
(c) if so, the details of steps taken by
Government to curb the unhealthy practice?
Drip irrigation system in U.P.
5403. SHRI HARENDRA SINGH
MALIK: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether any target had been fixed
for setting up of drip irrigation system in
Uttar Pradesh during the Ninth Five Year
Plan;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the financial assistance provided to
Uttar Pradesh during that period for the said
work;
(d) whether the above target has been
achieved;
(e) if not, the reasons therefor; and
(f) the target fixed by Government for
the Tenth Five Year Plan including funds
allocated for the said purpose?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

Agriculture extension services
5404. MISS MABEL REBELLO: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) what steps are envisaged to revitalize
the extension services in States;
(b) whether Government would
consider supporting the setting up of
regional/district agriculture training centres
for farmers and extension works by
funding through a special programme for
the purpose;
(c) whether the States spend a large
amount on salaries of extension personnel,
but they lack infrastructure, and lack of
funds has reduced the effectiveness of the
extension services;
(d) if so, what steps Government
envisage to support States; and
(e) whether a special Central scheme is
being considered in this regard?
Conversion of barren land into
agricultural land
†5405. DR. A. K. PATEL: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased to
state:
(a) the names of schemes under
implementation, State-wise, to convert the
barren land into agricultural land;
(b) whether it is also a fact that various
schemes to convert the barren land into
cultivation land are not being
implemented fully through time-bound
action plan;
(c) if so, the  reasons therefor,
State-wise; and
(d) the steps being taken by Government
to ensure time-bound implementation of
those schemes?
Supply of spurious Seeds, fertilizers etc.
5406. SHRI H. K. JAVARE GOWDA:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that due to supply
of spurious seeds, fertilizers and pesticides,
the farmers in the country are incurring
losses;
(b) if so, the details of companies/
agencies involved in supplying spurious
seeds, fertilizers and peticides during the
last three years; and
(c) the cases filed against spurious seeds,
fertilizers and pesticides suppliers in
Karnataka and the value of confiscated
seeds, fertilizers and pesticides for the last
three years?
Impact of agricultural trade reforms
on prices
5407. SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether a survey conducted by the
National Council on Applied Economic
Research has indicated that agricultural trade
reforms are likely to push up prices of
cereals as compared to other grains;
(b) whether the survey has also pointed
out that this would adversely affect the
poorer segments of both the rural and urban
society;
(c) if so, what are the other points made
in the survey report;
(d) whether Government have
considered the survey report; and
